expr: (with-temp-buffer (insert "a b a b a") (goto-char (point-min)) (condition-case e (list (re-search-forward "a" nil t 2) (point) (re-search-forward "a" nil t 5) (point)) (wrong-number-of-arguments (car e))))
note: THE ARGUMENT THAT STAYS A NAMED ERROR, with its condition name proved rather than assumed. Emacs answers (6 6 nil 6): COUNT repeats the search, a COUNT that overshoots fails like any other failed search (nil, and with NOERROR t point does not move). kg answers `wrong-number-of-arguments' -- the exact symbol, caught by name here so the record is a VALUE and the case reads as `this is the error you get' rather than as a condition record. Measured demand: no s.el call passes COUNT, and the frontier probe asserts `(re-search-forward 3)' as the arity it wants. THE DECISION, MADE: F.1 binds NOERROR (the third argument) and stops there; a fourth argument keeps raising this exact condition, and this case is written to STAY DIVERGENT.
